newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: TransAlta ahead of schedule on merger.
newsitem.headline: TransAlta ahead of schedule on merger.

text.p: Wellington power company TransAlta New Zealand's NZ$7.2 million profit for the half-year to March 31 was ahead of forecasts, and it said it expects to achieve full merger benefits a year ahead of schedule, the New Zealand Press Association report on Thursday.
The company had forecast a profit of $4.2 million for the first period after last year's merger of Capital Power and EnergyDirect.
TransAlta's result was announced after the market closed, but the company's shares ended up 1c at $1.83.
Chairman Ron Arbuckle said the merger process was taking place much faster than the two to three years expected.
The merger project probably would come in 12 months ahead of schedule and hence so would the benefits of that work, he said.

The latest result was boosted by lower-than-expected interest rates for the period and $1 million less in depreciation charges as no depreciation was recorded against assets up for sale. There had also been less capital spending than expected.

TransAlta NZ, 63 percent owned by Canada's TransAlta Corp, has about $330 million in debt and interest costs for the period were $15 million. Interest rates were about 1 percent lower than expected, implying an interest cost saving of about $1.5 million during the half year.

Arbuckle said the profit was considerably down on the result for the two component companies in the same period last year. But the big changes to the company since the merger made comparisons difficult.
About 200 staff have been laid off since October 1, leaving a staff of 330.
The company made a provision of $17.8 million last year to cover the three-year costs of merger such as redundancy payments.
It charged $9 million against that provision over the past six months, but that did not affect the bottom-line result.
Despite the better-than-expected profit the company did not declare a dividend. TransAlta decided some time ago that it would not pay a dividend for the six-month period.
Arbuckle said that the profit would have meant only a small dividend among more than 25,000 shareholders. Instead, the money would be put back into customer service improvements.

One blot on the copy book was the $560,000 loss in the period from TransAlta's quarter share in power trading company Pacific Energy. The trader had been forecast to make a $500,000 profit for TransAlta, but was caught by the rising spot price of power.
Operating revenues were only slightly higher than forecast at $125.5 million, but the company's pre-tax operating surplus was up $5.25 million at $13.45 million.
Tax was higher at $5.68 million against the $4.5 million forecast.
